metadata.title: Global motivation to learn and adult learning: A nomological network analysis and a four-year longitudinal study

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: Study 2 uses the German PIAAC 2012 sample and its longitudinal extension PIAAC-L (waves 2015 and 2016). The authors explicitly state that latent-variable models for MtL and openness were estimated in MPlus while considering sampling weights and replicate weights, and that literacy is incorporated via a plausible value (PV) approach with 10 PVs. For the binary participation outcomes (PAE indicators), models are fit with WLSMV using a probit function and pair-wise deletion, and model fit is evaluated using SRMR because replicate weights are used. Study 1 is based on a convenience panel (SoSci Panel) and does not describe complex survey weighting; therefore, the weighting logic primarily applies to the PIAAC/PIAAC-L longitudinal analyses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Study 1: convenience sample from the SoSci Panel; participants completed an online questionnaire in <10 minutes on average (N=747). Missingness was low (below 0.3%) and most variables had complete data; no additional exclusion rule is described beyond the reported low missingness. Study 2: starts from the German PIAAC 2012 sample (N=5465 adults aged 16–65). For longitudinal analyses, participants were included if they participated again in 2015 (t2) and/or 2016 (t3), with N=2502 at t2 and N=2370 at t3. Participants enrolled in part-time or full-time education in the year of the PAE measure (current/past 12 months) were excluded from analyses. For modeling, WLSMV uses pair-wise deletion for binary outcomes/predictors, and planned PAE has missingness by design (only asked to those not participating in the past 12 months).

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PIAAC 2012 the study leveraged Age, Sex, Level of education (ISCED) to predict predict subsequent PAE, finding that This paper investigates global motivation to learn (MtL) using the MtL scale implemented in the OECD Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC). Study 1 (SoSci Panel convenience sample; N=747) tests a nomological network via confirmatory factor analysis and bivariate associations between MtL and motivational/personality constructs, and reports that MtL shows strong convergent correlations with mastery goal orientation, intrinsic task value, need for cognition, and academic self-concept, with smaller associations with openness and conscientiousness and a small negative association with agreeableness. Study 2 uses the German PIAAC 2012 sample and its longitudinal extension PIAAC-L (t1=2012, t2=2015, t3=2016; N=5465 at baseline, N=2502 at t2, N=2370 at t3) to test prospective predictive validity of MtL for participation in adult education and training (PAE) over up to four years. The authors estimate latent-variable models in MPlus with sampling weights, replicate weights, and literacy incorporated through 10 plausible values; binary participation outcomes are modeled with WLSMV (probit) and pair-wise deletion, while planned PAE uses FIML. Across multiple models, MtL is a significant positive predictor of PAE in most specifications, but effects attenuate when literacy is included; openness does not significantly predict subsequent PAE. Limitations include reliance on latent-variable modeling rather than ML prediction, and the fact that predictive associations do not establish causal effects. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: The study is not an empirical machine-learning prediction paper: it uses confirmatory factor analysis and latent-variable regression/probit models to test construct validity (Study 1) and prospective predictive validity (Study 2). Consequently, no supervised ML algorithms are trained or compared, so ml_techniques is empty and main_findings is not populated under the ML-specific schema. The paper still provides quantitative longitudinal results (standardized probit coefficients and SRMR/R2), but these are from conventional latent-variable modeling rather than ML predictive modeling.
